name: Ghanshyam (course 2022 + 9:20 interview): candles, 9:20, 2:20, Fibonacci, breakouts
source: Ghanshyam option-buying course transcript (72 pages, 2022) + Face-to-Face 9:20 interview (5 Nov 2026), shared by Mandeep
about: One file for every Ghanshyam strategy (Mandeep, 12 Nov 2026: merge the 9:20 file into the course file, keep the better version). 9:20: from the interview file only the versions that did best in the 5-year Lab are kept (920-E: yesterday's high / low taken out inside the first candle with the 3-day trend, entry 09:25: +Rs 104 / +430 / +843 per trade, small samples) plus the course's own rule (big gap of 0.7%+ against the 3-day trend, first candle the opposite colour) and the plain with-trend break as the control; 920-A to D are dropped here (they lost in the Lab; recorded in the project notes). Course fixes in v2: Fibonacci only after a fall of 1%+ (his '300 points is weak' was ~0.7%); the 2:20 'middle of the range' is now the 5 candles before the 2:20 candle, as he said (the 13:00-14:15 version stays as the data version); breakouts need 3+ touches, a wait at the level and no long run into it (new facts lv_touches, lv_pause, lv_run). Thresholds are his rules scaled to today's prices (100-150 Bank Nifty points at ~42,000 = ~0.3%); example-day numbers are illustrations. Every strategy is on trial (test bench + the Ghanshyam paper account on Nifty and Bank Nifty); nothing reaches the alerts or the main account until it passes the Lab on unseen data and you switch it on.

strategies.note: Best 9:20 version in the 5-year Lab (+Rs 104 / +430 / +843 per trade on 65 / 16 / 9 trades, momentum exit): not proof.

strategies.name: 9:20 put: y'day low taken in 1st candle, downtrend (09:25)
strategies.note: Holdout positive, train negative in the 5-year Lab; on trial.

strategies.name: 9:20 call: uptrend, gap-down 0.7%+, green 1st candle
strategies.note: Course V2: uptrend + gap-down of 300-500 points (~0.7-1.2% then), first candle must be green, enter on the break of its high, stop at its low. The interview file used a 0.3% gap and lost; this is the stricter course version. Rare (he says ~6 days a year).

strategies.note: Course V2 mirror.

strategies.name: 9:20 plain call with the trend (control)
strategies.note: Control: the plain with-trend break lost after option costs in the 5-year Lab.

strategies.name: 9:20 plain put with the trend (control)
strategies.note: Control.

strategies.name: Shooting star after a rise, gap-down day (full size)
strategies.note: Course V1: trading below yesterday's close, a rise of 100-150 points from the open, a shooting star at the day's high; buy puts when a close breaks its low (within 3 bars); stop above the star; book when a candle closes above the previous one. Claim '8 of 10': not supported (51% win, n 35 on 2022-2026), but the best candle lead.

strategies.name: Shooting star, above yesterday's close (half size)
strategies.note: Course V1: the same star after price climbed back above yesterday's close: he trades half size (lower accuracy).

strategies.name: Hammer after a fall, gap-up day (full size)
strategies.note: Course V1: trading above yesterday's close, a fall of 100-150 points from the open, a hammer at the day's low; buy calls when a close breaks its high; stop below the hammer. Claim '90% over 100 trades': not supported (31-33% win, negative 2022-24 and 2025-26). Kept on trial so the Lab records it.

strategies.name: Hammer after a fall, below yesterday's close (half size)
strategies.note: Course V1: the hammer after price fell below yesterday's close: half size.

strategies.name: Hammer at yesterday's close (support)
strategies.note: Course V2: a hammer at yesterday's close (support) 'works very well'. Within 0.15% of yesterday's close.

strategies.name: Shooting star at yesterday's close (resistance)
strategies.note: Course V2 mirror: a shooting star at yesterday's close (resistance).

strategies.name: 2:20 call against the morning (13:00-14:15 range)
strategies.note: Course V3: break of the 14:15-14:20 candle's high, stop at its low, out on a close below the previous candle or by ~15:00; not when the candle sits in the middle of the afternoon range; a break against the earlier trend moves better. Best 2:20 lead in the check (+Rs 150 / -730 / +370 per trade), not proven.

strategies.name: 2:20 put against the morning (13:00-14:15 range)
strategies.note: Course V3 mirror: break of the 2:20 candle's low after a rising morning.

strategies.name: 2:20 call against the morning (course: 5-candle range)
strategies.note: Course V3, fixed in v2: 'if the 2:20 candle forms in the middle of the afternoon range (4-5 candles) no trade': the range is now the 5 candles before it.

strategies.name: 2:20 put against the morning (course: 5-candle range)
strategies.note: Course V3, fixed in v2: 'if the 2:20 candle forms in the middle of the afternoon range (4-5 candles) no trade': the range is now the 5 candles before it.

strategies.note: Does the Bank Nifty idea carry over to Nifty? (the course is Bank Nifty only) (v2: middle of the 5 candles before the 2:20 candle, as in the course)

strategies.name: AVOID check: 2:20 call with the morning move
strategies.note: Control: the same break in the direction of the morning move lost money in every period (-Rs 250 to -630 per trade). Expected to fail; kept to confirm the 'avoid' check on new data. (v2: middle of the 5 candles before the 2:20 candle, as in the course)

strategies.name: AVOID check: 2:20 put with the morning move
strategies.note: Control, mirror. (v2: middle of the 5 candles before the 2:20 candle, as in the course)

strategies.name: Fibonacci 0.71 call after a 1%+ fall
strategies.note: Course V5, fixed in v2: only after a strong fall (he calls 300 points 'weak' = ~0.7% then; 1%+ here). Buy calls when price crosses back above the 0.71 retracement; stop 0.38; T1 the high (~0.9R), T2 the 1.27 extension (~1.7R).

strategies.name: Fibonacci 0.71 put after a 1%+ rise (our mirror)
strategies.note: He uses Fibonacci for calls only and never tested puts: our own trial.

strategies.name: Breakout: 3+ touches, wait, no long run, trend (call)
strategies.note: Course V4, fixed in v2: today's high touched 3+ times, price waits near it (2+ candles = 10+ minutes), did not arrive after a long run (under 0.5% in the hour before), then a close above it; full size with the trend. His claim '7 of 10 with a pause' is what this tests.

strategies.name: Breakdown: 3+ touches, wait, no long run, trend (put)
strategies.note: Course V4 mirror: today's low.

strategies.name: Breakout after a long run (control: likely fails)
strategies.note: Control: he says a breakout after a long journey (300+ points then, ~0.7%) usually fails.
